# P212 contract-only outer source contract

Status: SOURCE_PREPARED / HOLD_OPERATIONAL. The exact prospective execution-state
amendment source is pinned; its independent root acceptance remains required.
No runtime probe, host dependency query,
driver import, AST/syntax check, kpsewhich invocation, binding enablement,
build, scientific run, Git write or external action occurred in this work.
The disabled companion is descriptive input only, not a future enabled binding.

## Fixed first action and finite successor gates

The only operational entry proposed here is one fresh contract01 invocation
of the received dependency driver under one supervisor. The inner driver may
run exactly `/usr/bin/kpsewhich --help`, followed by
`/usr/bin/kpsewhich --version`. It may not accept its own installed-option
semantics. A successful result does not authorize lookup, body reads, TeX,
BibTeX, ldd, building, science, a dependency lock or an external action.

The original STAGED_CAPTURE_AND_CLOSURE phase contract remains controlling.
Its lookup01 and bodies01 are independent future bindings with independent
receipts; these five new source files implement neither successor. Reusing
this outer source for another phase requires a separate source delta and
reception, not changing `phase` in a JSON file.

The old joint dependency-source root receipt remains an accepted historical
baseline. The prospective amended driver and companion hashes are exact
source dependencies of this packet. The amended driver is not accepted merely because
its author prepares it: an independent `source_amendment` receipt must later
exist and be fully pinned in the new outer binding before operation.

## What each source does

| Source | Restricted job |
|---|---|
| outer_contract.py | Full external binding reception, complete pre-Node input key, one Node spawn, subreaper-owned lifecycle, raw capture and after-key; no auto signal or seal |
| node_preload.js | Exact Node startup/settings observations, whole mapped-file/builtin keys, exact two cp.spawn vectors and native events; not a prestartup attestation |
| product_capture.js | One real exec_command and same-session empty write_stdin polls; preserve actual values and unknown handles; no file writes or next phase |
| python_runtime_probe.py | Separately authorized runtime-only import/path/ABI enumeration, statx and subreaper readback; no driver import or child spawn |
| node_runtime_probe.js | Separately authorized six-builtin import/map/source enumeration; no preload/driver load or child spawn |

No new source was executed or imported for preparation. Source inspection is
not a successful probe or correctness test. The Python supervisor imports
before it can read an internal binding; the external startup gate below is
therefore indispensable.

## Finite nonrecursive binding graph

The root first receives source and fresh runtime/bootstrap evidence. It then
writes a prepared Node-only request record: its literal argv contains the
future inner binding pathname, not the bytes or hash of either binding.
That prepared request is not an actual native tool result.

The enabled inner binding pins the amended driver and complete amended
companions, the prepared Node request, outer source, preload and relevant
input key. The enabled outer binding pins that complete inner binding and all
other dependencies. The outer binding does NOT list itself in `inputs`.
Its complete descriptor is supplied as the final literal interpreter argument
in the later actual product request. Thus Python's keyed `orig_argv_prefix`
excludes only that final descriptor; the actual complete argv is recorded.

The actual product request consequently depends on the final outer binding,
but no earlier receipt/binding depends on the actual product request bytes.
Future `product_startup` receipt means a received independent bootstrap key
and intended fixed invocation prefix, not a post-launch or self-referential
claim to have captured the final product return. Actual enclosing
functions.exec/yield/wait/final and exec_command/write_stdin originals are
attached finitely by root after the actual event, before final reception/seal.

## Enabled outer binding interface

Only root may create the future physical file
`qa/p212_build_dependency_outer_binding01/contract01/BINDING.json`.
The source enforces its schema `p212-contract-outer-binding-v1`, status
`ROOT_BOUND_CONTRACT_ONLY`, boolean enabled true, phase contract and these
exact top-level keys:

`schema, status, enabled, phase, output, inner_binding, node_preload, python,
runtime, inputs, receipts, policy, forbidden`.

References are exactly `{path,pin:{bytes,sha256}}`. The output is
`qa/p212_build_dependency_outer_capture01/contract01`; the inner binding is
`qa/p212_build_dependency_binding01/contract01/BINDING.json`; the native
query cwd is the existing, physically verified empty
`qa/p212_build_dependency_query01/query_cwd`. Neither output may exist at
entry or appear as immutable input. Root creates only needed physical parent
directories under separate preparation authority and keys them as ancestors.
No source in this packet probes or creates those future locations now.

The five receipt roles are `dependency_source, source_amendment, outer_source,
runtime, product_startup`. Each entire actual receipt is a bound receipt file.
The first is the exact old accepted baseline; the amendment receipt must also
equal the inner binding's driver_source reference. Receipt text is an external
root decision, not an automatically accepted label. The other four cannot
be filled with the historical baseline or an author preparation.

`python` contains exactly executable_resolved, orig_argv_prefix, sys_path,
version, mapped_paths, modules. The argv prefix is the literal interpreter
spelling, -I -S -B -X pycache_prefix=<fixed never_created_cache>, outer source
and fixed outer binding pathname. The cache must really remain absent.
`modules` maps every file-backed sys.modules name to its absolute path and
whole pin; `__main__` is the outer source, not the runtime probe source.
Do not relabel a probe's main module without this explicit received source
substitution. Mapped paths and module names are complete finite sets, never
counts borrowed from an earlier run.

`runtime` contains exactly node, native_request_ref, tool_closure.
The Node object contains executable_spelling, executable_resolved,
mapped_paths, builtin_source_fingerprints, versions, architecture, platform,
internal_bindings. Whole builtin registry entries are typed string
fingerprints, except an actually observed undefined configs slot. Every
NativeModule must belong to that fully keyed registry. Each Internal Binding
must belong to an explicitly received finite policy; an unobserved lazy
binding must be justified from received source/native image, not fabricated
as a probe observation. Complete native file and configuration closure remains
a separate received obligation. Tool closure explicitly includes kpsewhich,
all applicable ELF dependencies/aliases, loader/configuration inputs and
relevant absence/membership states, not a P211 TeX-domain alias.

The prepared Node request's exact object is specified in outer_contract.py.
It records the same literal argv, ROOT cwd, ENV8, umask 077, explicit bound
/dev/null stdin, exclusive two outer raw stream names, detached session and
close_fds=true used by the actual Popen call. Its
not_an_actual_product_tool_result is true. It is received under role receipt.

Each input descriptor has the accepted driver's exact ten fields:
path, role, kind, comparison, lstat, stat, resolved, symlink_target, content,
members. Only source/runtime/configuration/ancestor/cwd/receipt/device roles
are admitted here. No body/query_result route exists. Every alias, referent
and namespace ancestor must be explicit; complete regular bytes are pinned.
Missing placeholders, incomplete alias chains and implicit unkeyed maps fail.
Directory identity comparisons exclude content lifecycle fields only for
ancestor directories; all fourteen original integer stat fields are still
recorded. Stable comparisons intentionally permit atime changes only.

The external selected-binding descriptor is independently supplied outside
the selected binding. It must describe a physical regular configuration file
with no symlink and a nonnull full pin. Complete original raw bytes,
lexical/handle metadata and all fourteen stat fields are retained before and
after the complete native lifetime. statx also retains the actual 256-byte
buffer, returned mask and attribute masks. Birthtime absence is HOLD, never
a zero-valued stand-in. The JSON decimal fields remain integers as strings.

## Actual product and startup boundary

The proposed product request uses /bin/bash with login=false and tty=false,
then an explicit exec /usr/bin/env -i and exactly ENV8 before Python.
The env -i action does NOT prove that the already-started shell had a cleared
environment. The product_startup gate must independently receive the actual
shell/bootstrap executable, loader, relevant inherited startup environment
(including BASH_ENV/ENV/SHELLOPTS/BASHOPTS and LD_* effects), configuration
files/absence states, and product invocation. If product provenance cannot
establish this before launch, HOLD; do not fill that gap with a later ENV8
observation. Bash, env, Python and both lexical/resolved paths are keyed.

Before Node starts, the supervisor reads/hashes the entire approved input
universe, checks Python modules/maps/settings and explicit tool closure,
then sets umask 077, owns exclusive capture files and passes an exact ENV8.
The Node preloader cannot retroactively attest Node's executable/loader,
configuration or builtin bootstrap. Its observations must match the earlier
received full key and are retained again at exit.

The collector records the exact exec_command request before invoking it,
then each actual returned object and exact empty-stdin poll request/return.
It never makes up a session id, final exit or original tool envelope. It
returns actual captured values for finite root attachment with apply_patch
after an exclusive destination check; no replay is required just to attach.
The surrounding functions.exec request/yield/cell/wait/final values remain
root-owned and must be attached separately from their actual originals.
A thrown tool call has a JS catch record, not an invented native exit.

## Settlement, failures and acceptance limit

The supervisor sets and reads back Linux child-subreaper status before the
single Node spawn, sets a waitable SIGCHLD disposition, and starts Node in
a separate native session. It records discrete own task/children chains,
raw proc stat identity/start ticks, actual waitid WNOWAIT observations and
actual waitpid status. Final stream hashes require Node exit 0, actual ECHILD,
a final sampled empty own-descendant chain, only the expected Node reaped by
this supervisor, and completed inner and Node records for exactly both calls.

This is materially broader ownership than the inner native query PGID:
orphaned descendants can reparent to the living subreaper. It is NOT a census
of every process sharing an SID, an exhaustive historical spawn trace,
continuous tracing, or proof excluding escaped/duplicated external writers.
The kernel children interface is racy; disappearance or inconsistent identity
fails closed and is preserved, not smoothed into an inferred successful trace.
An unexpected adopted descendant requires root disposition even if reaped.

The outer deadline is 600 seconds; the product collector deadline is
660 seconds, with short empty polls. Unknown membership, missing close,
truncation, changed dependency, unreceived native module, nonzero exit,
signal or any failed check means no success/outer seal and no automatic
retry, signal, cleanup, lookup or body action. Source exceptions close only
owned descriptors. On an unresolved supervisor timeout it may exit without
settling descendants: this is explicitly UNKNOWN, not lifetime closure; root
must retain the actual process/session handle and perform a separately scoped
settlement decision. Neither timeout nor an absent later proc entry permits
retrospective final stream hashing.

Even the normal supervisor result is
CONTRACT_OUTER_CLOSED_ROOT_PRODUCT_RECEPTION_PENDING. It carries no outer
manifest. Root must receive original requests/results, full before/after
keys, raw stream and binding originals, actual session/process closure,
complete inner output and option-semantics findings. Only then may root
issue and seal a nonself capture reception. This still opens no next phase.

143	## Actual product and startup boundary
   144	
   145	The proposed product request uses /bin/bash with login=false and tty=false,
   146	then an explicit exec /usr/bin/env -i and exactly ENV8 before Python.
   147	The env -i action does NOT prove that the already-started shell had a cleared
   148	environment. The product_startup gate must independently receive the actual
   149	shell/bootstrap executable, loader, relevant inherited startup environment
   150	(including BASH_ENV/ENV/SHELLOPTS/BASHOPTS and LD_* effects), configuration
   151	files/absence states, and product invocation. If product provenance cannot
   152	establish this before launch, HOLD; do not fill that gap with a later ENV8
   153	observation. Bash, env, Python and both lexical/resolved paths are keyed.
   154	
   155	Before Node starts, the supervisor reads/hashes the entire approved input
   156	universe, checks Python modules/maps/settings and explicit tool closure,
   157	then sets umask 077, owns exclusive capture files and passes an exact ENV8.
   158	The Node preloader cannot retroactively attest Node's executable/loader,
   159	configuration or builtin bootstrap. Its observations must match the earlier
   160	received full key and are retained again at exit.
   161	
   162	The collector records the exact exec_command request before invoking it,
   163	then each actual returned object and exact empty-stdin poll request/return.
   164	It never makes up a session id, final exit or original tool envelope. It
   165	returns actual captured values for finite root attachment with apply_patch
   166	after an exclusive destination check; no replay is required just to attach.
   167	The surrounding functions.exec request/yield/cell/wait/final values remain
   168	root-owned and must be attached separately from their actual originals.
   169	A thrown tool call has a JS catch record, not an invented native exit.
